steps.title: Describe the outcome
steps.human: When I press the button, set SYS NEO Blue, send one PING to the test device at 0x5557, then set SYS NEO Black after PacketEnqueued. Blue marks the local operation in progress; it is not a delivery confirmation.
core: Reuse SYS BUTTON, SYS NEO and LORA SEND. The application coordinates them through existing events and commands.
This teaching scenario is independent of the package currently open. The supplied v3.1.5.14 pair also contains later ACK/WDG behavior.
Use 0. Power ON for startup setup. This example displays only the per-PRESS sequence; its exported task remains complete.
steps.meaning: Define the observable status transition first: Blue → local SEND operation → Black. Reuse existing resources.

steps.title: Preserve the PRESS context

The application validates input before any send. It must not allocate a second ctx for the same operation.

steps.title: Set Blue and send PING
steps.human: Set SYS NEO Blue immediately on the valid PRESS action. If that succeeds, Publish LORA SEND with the configured peer and PING #<counter>. Keep the same ctx.
core: NEO SET holds the color until another SET. Use the registered NeoHandler in SYS; another module uses Publish to SYS.
SEND accepts destination and payload. The synchronous response covers queue acceptance only; transmission is performed by the independent LORA worker.

value.success: Trace response; proceed to SEND only for a nonnull +OK response. Otherwise trace and stop.

value.result: Trace the response. PacketEnqueued means TX queue acceptance only. Preserve SEND failure and continue to finally Black cleanup.

declarations.meaning: Ordered application actions: SET Blue, then SEND. Guard SEND on Blue success. The next slide adds finally Black cleanup.

steps.meaning: Blue represents the interval during which the application executes SEND. There is no BLINK command and no guaranteed minimum visible duration.
runtimeKb: Record SET Blue result before publish_entry/SEND using the same ctx.
Record PacketEnqueued or failure separately; Blue alone is not queue acceptance.
logs: [TRACE] SYS:publish_entry ctx=08000004 dest=LORA cmd=SEND args=0x5557,PING #1 sync=True ...

steps.title: Set Black after the result
steps.human: After PacketEnqueued, set SYS NEO Black to end the local operation indication. Also attempt Black in finally when SEND fails or throws, provided Blue succeeded.
core: NEO SET Black switches the indicator off; it is not BLINK and adds no delay.
Finally cleanup preserves the existing application pattern. A NEO failure must not overwrite the original SEND outcome.

value.result: After Blue succeeded, run after SEND on success, error or exception. Trace response; retain the original SEND outcome if cleanup fails.

declarations.meaning: Status cleanup after SEND. Black is attempted on return or exception after successful Blue.

steps.meaning: Blue → Black brackets local command processing, not queue wait or remote delivery. A short interval may be hard to see physically.
runtimeKb: Record SEND result and subsequent SET Black response with the originating ctx.
If Black fails, retain both results. Do not erase the enqueue evidence.

steps.title: Observe queued transmission
steps.human: Let the existing radio worker process queued packets one at a time. Keep the wire packet format unchanged. This basic example does not wait for or act on any reply.
core: LORA owns TX serialization and QueueTX instrumentation. Reuse it; no additional application declaration is needed.
The worker can start TX before or after Black. The drawing groups responsibilities; it is not a deterministic thread schedule.
steps.meaning: QueueTX shows queue-worker progress; it is not proof of successful remote reception. A receiving-device log may supply separate evidence, but this example does not require it.
runtimeKb: Correlate QueueTX with SEND by ctx. Use timestamps to estimate queue delay at the existing trace checkpoint.
Do not label QueueTX as TX_DONE or an ACK. Exact air-start/air-end timing requires corresponding driver evidence.

workerBriefLines.text: Create the basic Pinging application using the existing SYS BUTTON, SYS NEO and LORA SEND contracts. Reuse board/HAL bindings, activation and module composition.
Keep the configured application test peer (default 0x5557) separate from the local radio address; retain the existing factory connector override.
At ApplicationStartUp, Publish SYS SUB with consumer SYS, topic /BUTTON/PRESS, filter $arg0>0|$tag=ping_on_press and delivery mode PUSH. Trace the response.

For each valid positive PRESS counter, preserve the event ctx and build PING #<counter> using the original validated counter text. Invalid input produces no resource action. The current integrated Button contract appends ctxXXXXXXXX in args[1]. Validate the positive counter at args[0] and accept this provenance argument; continue to use event ctx downstream.

On entry to the valid PRESS action, issue SYS NEO SET Blue and trace its result. Blue marks the local operation in progress; it does not indicate enqueue success or remote reception. If SET Blue fails, trace and stop before SEND.
Publish LORA SEND to the application test peer with the PING payload and the same ctx. Trace the returned result. PacketEnqueued confirms only acceptance into the TX queue.

After PacketEnqueued, issue SYS NEO SET Black with the same ctx and trace its result. Use finally cleanup to attempt Black on SEND error or exception as well, after the indication requested in L05 succeeded, so a failed operation does not leave a stale status. Preserve the original SEND result if cleanup fails.
Reuse the existing LORA worker: queued packets are processed for transmission one at a time. Keep the wire format unchanged. QueueTX is not TX_DONE or proof of remote reception.
Do not add SEND_ACK, ACK subscriptions, watchdogs, retry, or Green/Red response actions. Replace only the example-specific application workflow; retain unrelated declarations.

Use commands/events between modules. A same-module shortcut may call only the registered message handler with identical arguments, behavior and results to Publish; do not access private resource state.

Instrument startup/binding, event emission/delivery/handler, the status requested in L05, SEND result, Black cleanup and TX-queue progress. Retain timestamps, module and the operation ctx for Runtime Knowledge Base post-processing.

Declare a short impact smoke test: READY, one PRESS, the SET indication requested in L05, SEND/PacketEnqueued, SET Black, and the corresponding QueueTX checkpoint. Observe the physical indication separately; retain failure traces and note that worker TX may interleave with Black.

steps.title: Set Blue and issue SEND_ACK
steps.human: On entry to the valid PRESS action, issue SYS NEO SET Blue and trace its result. If SET Blue fails, stop before SEND_ACK. Blue indicates local command processing, not delivery. Publish LORA SEND_ACK with the same ctx and arguments: configured test peer, PING payload, SYS, ACK_*|$tag=blink_on_ack. Trace PacketEnqueued or failure. SEND_ACK ensures the missing exact /QRX/PACK consumer route before delegating to SEND; preserve all existing routes, including OFF, other modes and different filters. Do not overwrite or force-enable them.
core: SEND_ACK arguments are destination,payload,consumer,ackFilter. They contain no watchdog configuration.
Only a missing exact topic/consumer route is created PUSH. Existing routes are preserved regardless of creator, filter or mode. Other consumers have their own routes.

value.result: Trace enqueue or failure; preserve original result.

declarations.meaning: SET Blue gates SEND_ACK; route setup occurs before packet enqueue.

steps.meaning: A synchronous command result covers route preparation and queue acceptance, not ACK reception.
runtimeKb: First invocation: inspect route creation. Later invocation: confirm reuse without growing filters.
Record ESUB or send failure; SEND_ACK does not enqueue if subscription setup fails.

steps.title: End local indication and transmit
steps.human: After successful Blue, attempt SYS NEO SET Black in finally after SEND_ACK returns or throws. Preserve the original send result if cleanup fails. Black ends the local processing indication. Reuse the existing LORA TX queue: one packet at a time, independent of the application. QueueTX may interleave with Black. PacketEnqueued is queue acceptance; QueueTX is not TX_DONE or proof of remote reception.
core: SET Black is local cleanup; TX serialization belongs to LORA.
ACK timing and queue progress are independent; do not add sleeps to make Blue visible.

declarations.meaning: Finally cleanup after successful Blue.

steps.meaning: Blue → SEND_ACK → Black brackets local processing; Green is a later receive indication.
runtimeKb: Preserve send and cleanup results separately. Correlate QueueTX with PRESS by ctx.

steps.title: Receive ACK and indicate Green
steps.human: Handle LORA /QRX/PACK in SYS using the delivered blink_on_ack tag and existing event contract [from,to,RSSI,SNR,data] with the received packet ctx. Validate event shape and ACK_ payload prefix before SYS NEO BLINK Green,1,50. Trace both received data and the NEO result. Use the received ctx for these traces/actions.
core: LORA emits /QRX/PACK with [from,to,RSSI,SNR,data] and received TextPacket.Id as ctx.
VirtualModule filters/delivers the event to SYS. The application dispatches blink_on_ack and uses the existing NEO message handler.

value.input: Validate [from,to,RSSI,SNR,data] and ACK_ prefix; use received ctx.
value.semantics: Filtered reception indication only; no pending-operation confirmation or timeout.

declarations.meaning: Business ACK action, without timer access or confirmation.

steps.meaning: Green indicates a matching received ACK packet. It does not prove a unique pending request was completed.
runtimeKb: Capture QueueRX, emit/deliver/handler and Green result with received ctx.

workerBriefLines.text: Create Pinging with ACK and Watchdog from the explicitly selected VERIFIED pair. Derive the complete application delta from its actual contents: a Power ON pair needs Pinging+ACK+WDG; an Example 2 pair needs only the missing correlation/timeout behavior. Preserve HAL, resource activation, composition, unrelated modules, drivers, dependencies and unchanged source bytes. Complete output is not permission for full regeneration.

Keep the configured test peer (default 0x5557) separate from the local LoRa address and preserve the existing connector override/wire format. Use incoming event ctx for the supervised operation. This example provides request correlation, not sender authentication.

Keep startup from 0. Power ON: SYS SUB with consumer SYS, /BUTTON/PRESS, $arg0>0|$tag=ping_on_press, PUSH, tracing its result. Do not subscribe to ACK at startup: SEND_ACK establishes the missing exact consumer route on first use.

Accept a valid positive decimal PRESS counter in args[0], preserving its original validated text for PING #<counter>. Tolerate the appended OPEN lifetime marker ctxXXXXXXXX in args[1]; never use that marker as the supervised context. Invalid input is trace-only and performs no resource action.
For a valid PRESS issue SYS NEO SET Blue and trace its result. If Blue fails, stop before arming or sending. Blue indicates local command processing, not radio delivery.

Before SEND_ACK arm SYS TMR WDG synchronously using command ctx=event ctx and args WDG,ping_<ctx formatted X8>,15000,SYS,ping_timeout,ACK_PING #<counter>,blink_on_ack. Store expected reply and action through these public command arguments atomically with arm; no later private state writes or application pending table. Trace arm success/error. If arming fails or throws, report it and still attempt SEND_ACK; do not invent a pending operation.

Publish LORA SEND_ACK synchronously with the same ctx and arguments: configured peer,PING #<counter>,SYS,ACK_*|$tag=blink_on_ack. Preserve existing ACK subscriptions including different filters, modes and OFF; do not force-enable/overwrite. Trace PacketEnqueued or failure. SEND_ACK carries only its existing four arguments; watchdog configuration belongs to TMR WDG.

After successful Blue always attempt NEO SET Black in finally after the arm/send attempt, including failures; preserve original error information if cleanup fails. A successfully armed WDG remains armed after SEND_ACK failure and may expire. No retry is requested.

LoRa transmits one queued packet at a time. PacketEnqueued only acknowledges queue admission; QueueTX is not TX_DONE or peer reception. The 15000 ms deadline starts when WDG is armed, so it includes queue residence and radio/peer delay; do not dynamically adjust it or restart it on unrelated traffic.

For LORA/QRX/PACK delivered with blink_on_ack, validate the current event shape [from,to,RSSI,SNR,data], nonnull required fields and case-sensitive ACK_ prefix. Before any business action synchronously invoke SYS TMR WDG_CONFIRM with args WDG_CONFIRM,ping_<received ctx X8>,0x<received ctx X8>,SYS,blink_on_ack,<received data>. Parse the explicit accepted status in +DATA:<commandCtx>,SYS:tmr,wdg_confirm,<id>,accepted; generic +OK/ResultOk is insufficient. Only accepted may blink NEO Green,1,50 with received ctx. Atomic confirmation consumes/stops only its matched active unexpired WDG and reconciles its managed route.

Ignored/error/malformed ACK is trace-only: log ack_ignored with the reason and received ctx, without Green, retry, CANCEL, route mutation or other business action. Wrong ctx, exact reply mismatch (including a different counter), consumer/action mismatch, duplicate, missing pending operation and ACK at/past deadline must not be accepted. A wrong reply must not consume the valid pending operation. Correct ctx+exact expected payload within the deadline can be accepted even from a spoofed sender: correlation is not authentication.

On the committed SYS/WDG/EXPIRED event validate [id,tag,consumer], require id=ping_<event ctx X8>, tag=ping_timeout and consumer=SYS, then blink NEO Red,1,50 and trace it. The resource already committed expiration; do not CANCEL/rearm/close/confirm in this timeout handler. ACK acceptance and expiration are mutually exclusive terminal outcomes for one arm; late ACK cannot cause Green after Red.

Reuse the native managed WDG route per consumer: filter $arg2=SYS, stable while operations overlap. Resource lifetime/cleanup owns the route; the last active/delivering operation removes it when appropriate. ACK packet route is independent and remains reusable. Default TMR LIST hides idle/expired pool entries; retained standby storage is not an active operation.

All cross-module calls use Publish. Same-module shortcuts may invoke only registered command handlers with identical arguments/results. Generic TimerResource, VirtualModule and LoRa resources must contain no ping-specific prefix/payload/tag logic. Keep the application actions in small separate handlers and reuse existing atomic WDG_CONFIRM; no helper-only capability or new lock/state machine is requested.

Instrument timestamp,module,ctx,requested/expected reply, arm/send/confirm result, accepted/ignored reason and timeout as runtime Knowledge Base. Do not ask the user to interpret RKB: the worker derives results from captures; prompts are for physical actions or observations unavailable in RKB. Use explicit hexadecimal AT contexts. Add markers --- and worker expressions ### only according to the active test Role.

Return complete package1 and then package2 under normal phase gates. Preserve selected golden pair unchanged and reuse unaffected implementation byte-for-byte. Read the attached package0/task/Example3Acceptance.md and declare EXAMPLE3_WDG_ACK_IMPACT_SMOKE: compile/flash/startup, correct ACK before 15000 ms, silent peer timeout, wrong ctx/payload without consumption, duplicate/late ACK rejection, overlapping requests and route cleanup, managed route/filter isolation, and SEND continuation after a demonstrated WDG arm failure. Use controlled/fallback probes only when safe and available; report every unperformed case explicitly. Never claim full regression from smoke tests. Existing integrated Level0 sources need no zero patch.
